decisions.statement: The LLM never has broker access. Proposals go through the deterministic Risk Guardian, then the Execution Service.
Stop/pause/kill must work without the LLM (deterministic fast path).
3M candles are produced by resampling 1M because Capital.com has no 3-minute resolution.
HistData is used for hypothesis generation; Capital.com demo forward testing is used for confirmation. HistData is bid-only, M1, EST without DST; convert to UTC on import.
Start with one RunPod pod (ROLE=all, CPU only); split into core and worker, and move to managed Postgres/Redis, before live trading.

Telegram is the primary natural-language channel; the web UI is optional and sits behind the same ChatChannel interface. Decided by Claude on the owner's delegation: Telegram is the interface, with a web chat added later if wanted.
Strategies are declarative specs run in a sandbox; no LLM-written executable code runs in core or execution processes.
Backups: GitHub for code/config/state, HuggingFace for data and results. Never back up secrets.
Account size for risk sizing means account equity (balance plus open P&L).
Starting risk limits: 0.5% risk per trade, 2% max daily loss, 10% max drawdown, 3 concurrent live strategies.

Risk limits and Lab gates can be changed by the owner through natural language, but only via the deterministic SettingsService: allow-listed owner chat, confirmation, hard ceilings baked into the image, tightening immediate, loosening needs a second factor and a cooldown, no loosening while a loss halt is active. LLM agents cannot call or edit it.
GitHub namespace Tarek-Assaf; private repos. Proposed names: ai-trader (GitHub) and ai-trader-data (HuggingFace dataset). HuggingFace username confirmed as Tarek-Assaf.
Reports and alerts go through Telegram plus email (address and method pending, Q-006).

The earlier project is reference material. Fresh repo with the new architecture; audit the old project first (C-005) and adopt pieces selectively. Nothing is adopted without passing this project's tests and safety invariants, and any model or signal from it enters only through the Strategy Lab gates.
v1 timeframes: 1M, 3M and 5M. 3M is resampled from 1M; 15M can be added later through config.
Email reports use SMTP with an app password held as a RunPod Secret (REPORT_EMAIL_TO holds the recipient). Telegram stays the primary channel.
Hard ceilings in config/risk_ceilings.yaml: risk per trade 1.0%, daily loss 4%, drawdown 15%, concurrent live strategies 5.

Reuse of the earlier project follows docs/legacy_audit.md: adapt data QA, tick/spread handling, experiment logging, backtest structure and tests; skip its models, risk manager, paper engine, paper trades and requirements.txt. Models re-enter only through Strategy Lab gates.

Strategy Lab gates use the stricter minimums: Gate 1 at least 300 simulated trades (100 out-of-sample), 5 walk-forward windows, 3 validation periods; Gate 2 at least 4 weeks and 200 demo trades; Gate 3 at least 4 weeks and 100 micro-live trades. Other gate criteria unchanged.

Analyst roster v1 as in ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.2: AI analysts (Technical, News and Macro, Critic, Performance) plus code analysts (indicator/pattern engine, execution quality, data quality, Risk Guardian). Instrument knowledge lives in config playbooks.

Phase 0 uses uv 0.6.3 with committed uv.lock and exact direct dependency pins. In ROLE=all, root entrypoint only prepares /workspace ownership, then supervisord, PostgreSQL, Redis and API run as the non-root trader user; PostgreSQL and Redis bind to loopback.

Publish the container image to the private GitHub Container Registry package ghcr.io/tarek-assaf/ai-trader for RunPod. Pull authentication uses a GitHub classic PAT scoped to read:packages; rotate by adding a replacement token to RunPod, confirming image pull and /health, then revoking the old token.

Testing-phase LLM strategy (no live trading): mixed tiers. Cheap tier (small in-pod model or Haiku 4.5) for news sorting, summaries and tagging; mid tier (Haiku 4.5 or Sonnet 5.5) for researcher, analyst and critic; Sonnet 5.5 for the final decision; strongest tier (Opus 5.5 or Fable 5.1) unused until the system is profitable. Event-driven invocation, prompt caching, batch mode for Lab and reports, hard daily spend cap. Provider and exact models remain swappable by config and are to be compared in a bake-off before live trading. No GPU role in v1.

Durable route for PAPER operation: keep PostgreSQL on the pod's container disk (POSTGRES_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ai-trader-pgdata or similar) and make it durable with logical backups to the network volume: pg_dump -Fc every 5 minutes and on SIGTERM to /workspace/backups (keep last 48, write to temp file then rename, verify with pg_restore --list), and automatic restore at startup when the data dir is empty and a valid dump exists. Redis may stay on /workspace (no mode-bit requirement; verify). Network volume stays the durable home for dumps, logs and data lake. Accepted loss window: up to 5 minutes of paper-trading rows after a crash. Before any live trading, move to managed PostgreSQL (D-005); this is not acceptable for live.
